fasti.note: Saturninus' second tribunate and Glaucia's praetorship: veteran colonies, oath to uphold the agrarian law; Metellus Numidicus exiled. Murder of the candidate Memmius; senatus consultum ultimum; Saturninus and Glaucia killed (December). Julius Caesar born (12 or 13 July 100; some argue 102).
The Marcus Antonius of this year is the Orator, grandfather of the triumvir. Metellus Numidicus recalled (98).
Lex Caecilia Didia: trinundinum between promulgation and vote; ban on omnibus bills (leges saturae).
Senatus consultum forbidding human sacrifice (Pliny NH 30.12). Censors Lucius Valerius Flaccus and Marcus Antonius.
Ptolemy Apion bequeaths Cyrene to Rome (organised as a province only in 74). Sulla propraetor in Cilicia meets the Parthian envoy Orobazus (96 or 92).
Lex Licinia Mucia sets up a quaestio to expel Italians illegally registered as citizens, a cause of the Social War. Scaevola, pontifex, governs Asia as a model administrator.
Censors Crassus and Domitius close the Latin rhetoric schools. Trial and condemnation of Publius Rutilius Rufus for extortion, an equestrian jury's revenge.
Tribunate of Marcus Livius Drusus: jury reform, colonies, and citizenship for the Italians; his laws annulled, and he is assassinated. The Social War begins at Asculum (late 91).
Social War: Rutilius killed at the Tolenus (11 June). Lex Julia grants citizenship to allies who stayed loyal or laid down arms. The Italian confederacy capital at Corfinium (Italia).

Cato killed at the Fucine Lake. Strabo takes Asculum; lex Pompeia gives Latin rights to the Transpadanes. Lex Plautia Papiria extends citizenship to individuals who registered within 60 days. Mithridates VI overruns Asia.

Asiatic Vespers: up to 80,000 Romans and Italians massacred (Valerius Maximus 9.2.3 ext.). Tribune Sulpicius transfers the Mithridatic command to Marius; Sulla marches on Rome with six legions, the first such march; Sulpicius killed. Pompeius Rufus murdered by Strabo's troops.
Cinna expelled by Octavius and deposed by the Senate; Merula (flamen Dialis) made suffect. Cinna and Marius besiege and take Rome; Octavius killed, Merula commits suicide. Sulla besieges Athens.

Marius died on 13 January in his seventh consulship. Sulla sacks Athens (1 March) and wins at Chaeronea and Orchomenus. Flaccus sent east with an army against both Mithridates and Sulla, murdered by Fimbria.
Peace of Dardanus between Sulla and Mithridates; Asia fined 20,000 talents.
Cinna killed by mutinous troops at Ancona; Carbo sole consul for the rest of the year.

Sulla lands at Brundisium; Pompey raises three legions in Picenum for him. Scipio's army defects at Teanum. Temple of Jupiter Capitolinus burns (6 July) with the Sibylline books. Second Mithridatic War (83-81, Murena).

The Younger Marius (aged 26 or 27) besieged at Praeneste and kills himself. Battle of the Colline Gate (1 November). Sulla named dictator legibus scribundis et rei publicae constituendae (interrex Lucius Valerius Flaccus, lex Valeria). Proscriptions. Carbo executed by Pompey in Sicily.

Sulla's laws: Senate enlarged to c. 600 with equestrians; jury courts given back to senators; tribunate gutted; cursus honorum regulated (quaestorship at 30, praetorship 39, consulship 42); quaestors 20, praetors 8; permanent quaestiones. Pompey's African campaign and first triumph (80 or 81).
Sulla holds the consulship while still dictator (he abdicated the dictatorship probably in 81 or 80). Sertorius in Spain invited by the Lusitanians. Cicero's Pro Roscio Amerino.
Sulla lays down power and retires to Puteoli. Servilius campaigns in Cilicia and Isauria (Isauricus), 78-74.
Sulla dies (spring) and receives a state funeral. Lepidus agitates to undo Sulla's settlement, leads a rising in Etruria; Tabularium completed by Catulus.
Lepidus defeated at the Milvian Bridge and Janiculum; dies in Sardinia. Pompey given proconsular imperium against Sertorius as a privatus.
Sertorius' alliance with Mithridates (75?). Battle of Lauron: Sertorius defeats Pompey.
Lex Aurelia permits ex-tribunes to stand for higher office. Caesar captured by pirates. Nicomedes IV bequeaths Bithynia (died 75 or 74).
Third Mithridatic War. Marcus Antonius (Creticus) given an extraordinary command against the pirates. Cyrene organised as a province.
Spartacus breaks out of the gladiatorial school at Capua. Lucullus relieves Cyzicus. Sertorius assassinated by Perperna (73 or 72).
Both consuls defeated by Spartacus; command given to Crassus as praetor/proconsul. Pompey ends the Sertorian war.
Crassus crushes Spartacus in Lucania; 6,000 crucified along the Via Appia. Pompey mops up fugitives. Lucullus overruns Pontus.

Pompey consul at 35 without any prior magistracy. Tribunate's powers restored. Lex Aurelia iudiciaria: juries shared among senators, equites and tribuni aerarii. Cicero prosecutes Verres. Censors expel 64 senators and register 910,000 citizens. Virgil born (15 October).
Lucullus defeats Tigranes at Tigranocerta (6 October). Metellus (later Creticus) begins the conquest of Crete (69-67). Capitoline temple rededicated by Catulus.
Metellus died early in the year; the suffect elected (Servilius Vatia?) died before taking office, and Marcius served alone (Dio 36.4). Lucullus' troops mutiny at Nisibis under Clodius' incitement.

Lex Gabinia gives Pompey an extraordinary command against the pirates (imperium over the sea and 50 miles inland, 500 ships, 24 legates); he clears the Mediterranean in three months. Lex Calpurnia de ambitu. Lucullus' army defeated at Zela (Triarius).

Lex Manilia (supported by Cicero, De imperio Cn. Pompei) gives Pompey the war against Mithridates and Tigranes. Pompey defeats Mithridates at Nicopolis (Dasteira). The so-called first Catilinarian conspiracy (late 66), largely a later fabrication.

The consuls-elect, Publius Autronius Paetus and Publius Cornelius Sulla, were convicted of electoral bribery and replaced by Cotta and Torquatus. Crassus as censor proposes enfranchising the Transpadanes and annexing Egypt. Horace born (8 December).
Pompey annexes Syria, ending the Seleucid monarchy. Senatus consultum dissolving collegia.

Conspiracy of Catiline; senatus consultum ultimum (21 October); Catilinarian orations; execution of five conspirators without trial (5 December). Pompey takes Jerusalem and enters the Holy of Holies. Mithridates dies at Panticapaeum. Caesar elected pontifex maximus. Octavian (Augustus) born 23 September.
Catiline killed at Pistoria (January). Pompey lands at Brundisium and disbands his army. Bona Dea scandal: Clodius at the rites in Caesar's house; Caesar divorces Pompeia.
Clodius acquitted after jurors bribed (Crassus' money). Pompey's third triumph (28-29 September). Caesar governs Hispania Ulterior.
Pompey, Crassus and Caesar form the informal coalition later called the first triumvirate (late 60 or 59). Helvetian unrest.

Caesar's agrarian laws; Bibulus withdraws to watch the heavens ('the consulship of Julius and Caesar'). Pompey's eastern acta ratified; Asian tax contract reduced by a third. Lex Iulia de repetundis. Lex Vatinia gives Caesar Cisalpine Gaul and Illyricum for five years; the Senate adds Transalpina. Pompey marries Julia. Ptolemy XII recognised as king. Livy born (59 or 64).
Clodius tribune: free grain dole, collegia restored, Cicero exiled (March), Cato sent to annex Cyprus. Caesar defeats the Helvetii at Bibracte and Ariovistus near Mulhouse.
Cicero recalled (4 August law; returns 4 September). Pompey given the cura annonae for five years. Caesar defeats the Belgae (the Sabis/Selle against the Nervii).
Conference at Luca (April) renews the coalition. Caesar's naval war against the Veneti. Cicero's Pro Sestio and De provinciis consularibus.

Lex Trebonia: five-year commands for Pompey (Spain) and Crassus (Syria); lex Pompeia Licinia extends Caesar's. Theatre of Pompey dedicated (first permanent stone theatre). Caesar bridges the Rhine and crosses to Britain. Gabinius restores Ptolemy XII.

Electoral bribery scandal (interest rates double). Death of Julia. Caesar's second British expedition; Cassivellaunus. Eburones destroy Sabinus and Cotta at Atuatuca. Crassus plunders the Jerusalem temple.
Elections delayed until July by rioting. Crassus killed after the defeat at Carrhae (June) by the Parthian Surena; eagles lost.

consuls: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius Scipio Nasica
fasti.note: Clodius killed by Milo's men on the Via Appia (18 January); Senate house burned. Pompey made consul sine collega (24 Intercalaris), takes Metellus Scipio as colleague from August and marries his daughter Cornelia. Laws on violence and bribery; five-year gap between office and province. Revolt of Vercingetorix; Gergovia; Alesia.
Marcellus has a Transpadane of Comum flogged to deny Caesar's grant of citizenship. Cicero proconsul of Cilicia.
Tribune Curio, bought by Caesar, vetoes his recall. Senate votes 370 to 22 that both Caesar and Pompey should lay down their commands (1 December); the consul ignores it and hands Pompey a sword.

Senatus consultum ultimum (7 January); Caesar crosses the Rubicon (10/11 January). Pompey and the consuls evacuate Italy. Caesar defeats the Pompeians at Ilerda; Massilia besieged; Curio killed in Africa. Caesar dictator for eleven days to hold elections. Different Gaius Claudius Marcellus from the consul of 50 (cousin).
Dyrrhachium; Pharsalus (9 August); Pompey murdered at Pelusium (28 September). Caesar besieged in Alexandria; library fire. Caesar named dictator (second, for a year).

No consuls for most of the year; Caesar dictator with Antony as master of horse governing Italy. Calenus and Vatinius elected in the autumn for the last three months (often listed as suffects; the Fasti treat them as the year's consuls). Battle of the Nile; Zela (2 August): 'veni, vidi, vici'. Mutiny of the legions in Campania.

Thapsus (6 April); Cato's suicide at Utica. Caesar dictator for ten years. Four triumphs. Calendar reform: the 'year of confusion' of 445 days, with the Julian calendar from 1 January 45. Forum of Caesar and temple of Venus Genetrix dedicated (26 September).

Caesar sole consul until October, then resigns to Fabius and Trebonius. Fabius died on 31 December and Caninius was made consul for the remaining hours, mocked by Cicero (Fam. 7.30). Munda (17 March) ends the Pompeian resistance in Spain.

Caesar dictator perpetuo (February); Lupercalia diadem (15 February); assassinated on the Ides of March (15 March) in the Curia of Pompey. Dolabella took his place. Octavian adopted by testament; Cicero's first Philippics.

War of Mutina: Hirtius killed at Mutina (21 April) and Pansa dies of wounds after Forum Gallorum. Octavian marches on Rome and is elected consul (19 August) aged 19 with his cousin Pedius, who died in office. Lex Titia (27 November) creates the triumvirate of Antony, Lepidus and Octavian for five years. Proscriptions; Cicero killed (7 December).
Divus Iulius consecrated (1 January). Battles of Philippi (October and 23 October): suicides of Cassius and Brutus. Sextus Pompey holds Sicily.
Veteran settlements in Italy cause mass confiscations (Virgil's Eclogues). Lucius Antonius and Fulvia lead resistance; Perusine War (41-40). Antony meets Cleopatra at Tarsus.

Fall of Perusia. Pact of Brundisium: Antony takes the East, Octavian the West, Lepidus Africa; Antony marries Octavia. Virgil's Fourth Eclogue dedicated to Pollio. Parthian invasion of Syria; Herod declared king of Judaea by the Senate. Balbus, from Gades, the first consul born outside Italy.
Treaty of Misenum with Sextus Pompey. Ventidius defeats the Parthians at the Cilician Gates and Mount Amanus. Pollio founds Rome's first public library.
Octavian marries Livia (17 January). Ventidius kills Pacorus at Gindarus (9 June). War with Sextus Pompey resumes; Octavian's fleet wrecked. Agrippa in Gaul crosses the Rhine; Ubii resettled.
Pact of Tarentum renews the triumvirate for five years. Agrippa builds the Portus Iulius at Lake Avernus. Herod takes Jerusalem. Varro's De re rustica.

Agrippa defeats Sextus Pompey at Mylae and Naulochus (3 September). Lepidus stripped of his triumviral powers, kept as pontifex maximus. Antony's Parthian expedition fails at Phraaspa; huge losses in retreat. Octavian receives tribunician sacrosanctity.
The consul Sextus Pompeius is a distant relative, not the son of Pompey, who was executed at Miletus this year by Antony's agent Titius. Octavian's Illyrian campaign (35-33); Siscia taken.
Antony resigned on 1 January. Antony annexes Armenia; Donations of Alexandria (autumn) assign territories to Cleopatra and her children.
Octavian appears as Imperator Caesar Divi filius. Agrippa as aedile restores the sewers and aqueducts and builds the Aqua Julia. Triumvirate lapses at year's end (or 32).

Both consuls, Antonians, flee to Antony with some 300 senators. Octavian reads Antony's will; oath of all Italy (tota Italia); war declared on Cleopatra alone. The suffect Lucius Cornelius is probably Cinna.
Messalla replaced Antony, who had been designated. Battle of Actium (2 September). Actian era begins. Octavian's consulships are continuous 31-23 BC.

Alexandria taken (1 August); suicides of Antony and Cleopatra; Egypt annexed under an equestrian prefect (Cornelius Gallus). The suffect Cicero, son of the orator, announced Antony's death to the Senate. Crassus (grandson of the triumvir) later wins the spolia opima claim in Thrace (29), denied by Octavian.
Triple triumph (13-15 August) for Illyricum, Actium and Egypt. Temple of Janus closed. Curia Julia and the temple of Divus Julius dedicated.
Census and lectio senatus (first since 70); 4,063,000 citizens (Res Gestae 8). Octavian princeps senatus. Restoration of 82 temples. Mausoleum begun. Illegal triumviral acts annulled.

Settlement of 13 January: Octavian returns the res publica and receives a ten-year provincial command (Spain, Gaul, Syria, Egypt) and, on 16 January, the name Augustus. Agrippa builds the first Pantheon. Augustus to Gaul and Spain.
Cantabrian War (26-19). Cornelius Gallus disgraced and commits suicide. Praefectus urbi Messalla resigns after six days.
Galatia annexed after Amyntas' death. Marcus Marcellus marries Julia. Aelius Gallus' expedition to Arabia Felix (26-24). Augusta Emerita and Augusta Praetoria founded.
Augustus returns from Spain, seriously ill.

Aulus Terentius Varro Murena appears in the Fasti Capitolini as the original colleague; whether he died before taking office or was condemned for conspiracy (the Caepio-Murena plot, perhaps 22) is debated (Swan; Badian). Augustus nearly dies; resigns the consulship (1 July) and receives tribunicia potestas and imperium maius: the 'second settlement'. Marcellus dies. Sestius, a former Brutus partisan, replaced Augustus.
Famine and plague; Augustus refuses the dictatorship and accepts the cura annonae. Trial of Marcus Primus.
Agrippa marries Julia. Electoral disturbances; Augustus in the East.

Parthian settlement: Phraates IV returns the standards lost by Crassus and Antony (12 May celebrated); Tiberius crowns Tigranes III in Armenia. Arch for the standards; temple of Mars Ultor on the Capitol.

Sentius sole consul for much of the year; disturbances over the election of Egnatius Rufus. Agrippa completes the subjugation of the Cantabri; Aqua Virgo. Deaths of Virgil (21 September, Brundisium) and Tibullus. Augustus receives consular imperium for life (per Dio).
Leges Iuliae on adultery and marriage (lex Iulia de maritandis ordinibus, de adulteriis coercendis). Augustus' powers renewed for five years; Agrippa given tribunicia potestas. Senate purged to 600.
Ludi Saeculares (31 May-3 June); Horace's Carmen Saeculare. Augustus adopts his grandsons Gaius and Lucius.
Clades Lolliana: Marcus Lollius loses the eagle of Legio V to the Sugambri. Augustus to Gaul (16-13).
Tiberius and Drusus conquer Raetia and Vindelicia; Alpine campaign. Piso is the Pontifex, patron of the poets.
Agrippa in the Black Sea; Bosporan settlement. The consul Lentulus is the Augur, said to be the richest man of his day.
Augustus returns from Gaul; Ara Pacis Augustae voted (4 July). Theatre of Balbus. Agrippa's tribunicia potestas renewed; Pannonian campaign.

Messalla Appianus died in office; Valgius replaced him, and Caninius (died) and Volusius followed. Augustus becomes pontifex maximus after Lepidus' death (6 March). Agrippa dies (March). Drusus' German campaigns begin; altar of Rome and Augustus at Lugdunum dedicated (1 August 12 or 10).
Tiberius forced to divorce Vipsania and marry Julia. Theatre of Marcellus dedicated (13 or 11).
Iullus, son of the triumvir, consul. Claudius born at Lugdunum (1 August).

Drusus reaches the Elbe, dies after a fall from his horse (September). Ara Pacis dedicated (30 January). Province of Asia adopts the Julian calendar with the year beginning on Augustus' birthday (Priene inscription).
Month Sextilis renamed Augustus. Deaths of Maecenas and Horace. Tiberius in Germany deports 40,000 Sugambri across the Rhine. Augustus' powers renewed for ten years; census of 4,233,000 citizens.
Rome divided into 14 regions and 265 vici with vicomagistri; cult of the Lares Augusti. Porticus of Livia dedicated.
Tiberius receives tribunicia potestas for five years but retires to Rhodes. Paphlagonia annexed.
Augustus resumed the consulship to introduce Gaius Caesar to public life (princeps iuventutis). Pairs of suffect consuls each year become regular from now.
Death of Herod the Great (spring 4 BC; some scholars argue 1 BC). Cyrene edicts of Augustus (7/6 BC) and the SC Calvisianum on extortion procedure (4 BC).

Augustus named pater patriae (5 February). Forum of Augustus and temple of Mars Ultor dedicated (1 August); naumachia. Julia exiled to Pandateria for adultery; Iullus Antonius forced to suicide. Lex Fufia Caninia limits testamentary manumission.
Gaius Caesar's eastern mission begins. The Piso of this year is the Augur. Year 1 BC is followed directly by AD 1 (no year 0).
